_comment: digigraph model POLICY — the model ids routing decisions are made from, not
resolved configuration. Loaded once at import time by model_config.py
(_load_model_policy), fail-loud: a missing or malformed file raises there rather
than degrading, because the failure modes are silent and wrong, not loud.
An absent or empty `flagship_model_id_markers` classifies EVERY model as
non-flagship, which would quietly re-route every phase model onto a tier that
was never cleared for it; an absent `fallback_model` leaves the mode ladder with
no last resort at all. Both raise (see ModelPolicyConfig's validators).
`fallback_model` is only reached when model_modes.yaml has no `default_model`
and no `defaults[mode]` for the active llm_mode. It is a different kind of value
from the markers — a single deployment default rather than a classification set —
so it is its own key, not a marker.
`balanced_flagship_markers` MAY be empty: that clears no frontier model for
`balanced`, which is the stricter direction. Only the flagship set is required.
Markers are matched as substrings of the lowercased slug, so they are family
prefixes (`claude-4`) rather than exact ids; they are stripped and lowercased on
load, since matching is case-insensitive.
Distinct from config/model_modes.yaml (per-deployment defaults, hot-reloaded on
mtime change, lenient) and config/byok-providers.json (the BYOK allowlist and its
user-facing model examples). This file is a routing POLICY: it changes at the pace
of a code review, not a redeploy, which is why it loads once at import.
